Subject: Clarifying per-request accounting and context subsumption for pilot usage

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Streamline is excited about the latency profile. Before we progress to contract terms, we need to validate how billing will work for our main usage patterns so we can model economics for our SRE and finance teams. Two quick items: one technical and one commercial.

1) Accounting questions (technical):
- We do a lot of short chat interactions (typical user messages ~10–40 tokens) but each session includes a long system prompt and an initial indexing prompt (~1,000–1,200 tokens). Will the long system prompt be re-billed for every API call or is there an automatic prefix/KV cache that stops recharging the same 1,200-token prefix?
- If KV caching is applied, is the billing reduced on input tokens for the subsequent calls or do you still bill full input size and only save on the model compute portion?
- How does rounding work? Our current provider rounds up to 100-token buckets which materially inflates costs for lots of short calls.

2) Commercial ask:
- For the pilot (expected ~500k requests/month, mostly short), could we get worked examples of the effective token billing under different policies (per-call per-token exact, per-call rounded-up buckets, and a small per-call minimum)? We attached a sample usage profile (pilot_usage_profile.csv) that shows session lengths and call counts by type.

Can you return a short worked example for 3 scenarios (baseline, with KV cache reuse, with rounding to X tokens) so we can plug into our TCO model? If you have a recommended default to avoid surprising customers, please call that out.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Lina Park
Head of Platform
Streamline.AI

Subject: Re: Clarifying per-request accounting and context subsumption for pilot usage

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear note and the CSV; this is exactly the right level of detail. Short answer up front: we bill tokens for input + output on each API call, but prefix/KV caching can materially reduce input billing when the cache is hit; rounding/minimums depend on plan type (hosted vs dedicated) and any pilot concessions.

Short breakdown so you have a working frame-of-reference:
- Token accounting model: billed_tokens = billed_input_tokens + billed_output_tokens. For hosted API the default is per-token counting with a configurable minimum and optional rounding band for high-volume pilots (we typically round to the nearest N tokens for aggregation efficiency).
- KV/prefix cache: if the request matches a cached prefix and is routed to the same cache slice, we do not re-bill the cached prefix tokens for input. In practice that means your large system prompt can be cached once per session/namespace and only the short user message + model output are billed on subsequent turns. If the request routes to a different cache shard (rare in cross-region fallbacks) we will charge the input tokens again unless we can fetch/cache the prefix.
- Rounding policy: default hosted behavior is to bill exact tokens, but we offer an optional rounding window for pilots (common defaults we negotiate: 10, 25, or 50 tokens). We avoid 100-token buckets unless the customer requests extreme smoothing.

To avoid back-and-forth, I'm preparing three worked examples using your CSV and the three policies you asked for. I'll loop Finance and Legal internally for the pilot concession.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll push a worked-examples spreadsheet back to you by EOD tomorrow.
- If you want the strong guarantee (cache residency for the system prompt) we should scope a pinned-session offering (small configuration change) — that carries a small operational commitment but will guarantee no re-billing of the system prompt.

I’ve attached an internal reference doc and will follow up with the three worked scenarios.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Clarifying per-request accounting and context subsumption for pilot usage — worked examples and confirmation

Hi all — quick finance confirmation and worked examples below. Laura — I kept legal phrasing minimal; we will record the cache credit as a billing credit (not an SLA) per Vanessa’s ask.

Pilot commercial terms (summary):
- Discount: 30% off list hosted token rate for first 90 days.
- Rounding: during pilot we will round up billed tokens to the nearest 25-token increment for hosted calls only.
- KV-cache credit: a one-time credit equal to the cost of 10,000 cached input tokens at list rate, applied to your first invoice at the end of month 1.

Assumptions used: list input+output rate = $0.0004 per token. Discounted rate = 0.00028 per token. Rounding increment = 25 tokens.

Worked examples (using sample rows from pilot_usage_profile.csv):

Scenario A — Initial session create (system prompt 1,150 tokens + user prompt 45 tokens -> model returns 60 tokens):
- Exact per-token (no rounding, no cache): billed = 1,150 + 45 + 60 = 1,255 tokens -> cost @ list = $0.502; discounted = $0.3514
- With KV cache (assume system prompt cached after first call): first call billed as above. Subsequent turn where user only sends 10-token message and gets 40-token reply: billed = 10 + 40 = 50 tokens -> cost @ discounted = 50 * 0.00028 = $0.014
- With rounding to 25 tokens: the 50-token call rounds up to 50 (already a multiple) so no extra in this example; a 7-token call would round to 25 tokens.

Scenario B — High-frequency short interactions (50,000 calls per day, average billed tokens per call after cache reuse = 35 tokens):
- Exact per-token monthly cost = 50,000 * 35 * 30 * 0.00028 ≈ $1,470,000 (discounted rate applied)
- With rounding to 25 tokens, each 35-token call rounds up to 50 tokens -> monthly cost ≈ 50,000 * 50 * 30 * 0.00028 ≈ $2,100,000. The rounding multiplier here is material; that’s why we chose 25 tokens (trade-off between smoothing and inflation).

Scenario C — Mixed-length burst with quantized model differences (system prompt tokenization varies; token counts may differ by ±10% between model variants):
- We recommend modeling a 10% buffer on large pre-prompts when forecasting cost for cross-model fallbacks. Quantization differences are orthogonal to rounding policy but will affect absolute token counts.

Operational notes:
- To deliver the guaranteed cache residency (zero re-billing of system prompt), we will operate pinned-session instances for your pilot. There is a small incremental operational cost (pro-rated into the discounted pilot fee) and we will document expected hit rates.
- Cache-credit mechanics: we’ll calculate the monetary value of 10,000 input tokens at list rate ($0.0004 * 10,000 = $4.00) and apply as a line-item credit; this is meant to offset initial churn when caches are warming.

Next steps:
- Vanessa: please share the full spreadsheet (streamline_billing_examples.xlsx) with the three scenario tabs — we used the sample rows to produce the above numbers.
- Lina / Alex: if the numbers look reasonable, we’ll prepare a short pilot amendment with the discount, rounding, and cache-credit language and send for signature.

Thanks — we’re happy to review any further permutations (different rounding bands, dedicated vs hosted economics).

-Markus
